coaching.summary: Take the bar from a rack onto the front of your shoulders with elbows pointing forward, squat until your hips sink below your knees, then stand back up.
cues: Keep the elbows high so the bar stays stacked on the shoulders.
Brace hard and sit straight down between the hips instead of folding forward.
Drive up with the chest tall and keep the rack position all the way through the rep.

introduction.title: What Makes the Front Squat Different
paragraphs: The front squat puts the bar across the front of your shoulders instead of your upper back. That one change keeps your torso far more upright, loads the quads harder, and asks your upper back and trunk to hold a strong position all the way down and back up.

Most lifters front squat less than they back squat, often around 80 to 85 percent of it once the front rack feels comfortable. The lighter load is kind to the lower back while still building serious leg strength, which is why the front squat is a favourite of athletes, weightlifters and anyone who wants a more upright squat.
Start light and own the rack position:

paragraphs.text: elbows high, bar resting on the shoulders, fingers relaxed

faqItems.question: How much should I front squat compared to my back squat?

faqItems.question: Is the front squat better than the back squat?
faqItems.answer: Neither is better, because they do different jobs. The back squat lets you move the most weight and trains the whole posterior chain. The front squat keeps you upright, emphasises the quads and upper back, and is gentler on the lower back. Many strong programs use both.

faqItems.question: What grip should I use for the front squat?
answer: The clean grip, with your fingers under the bar and elbows high, is the classic choice and carries over directly to the
. The crossed-arm grip suits lifters with tight wrists, and straps looped around the bar are a good middle ground while mobility improves.

faqItems.question: Why do my elbows drop in the front squat?
faqItems.answer: When the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward and pulls your chest down. Drive the elbows up as you leave the bottom, before the hips rise, keep the upper back tight, and choose a weight you can hold in position for every rep.

faqItems.question: How deep should I front squat?
faqItems.answer: Aim for your hips to sink below the top of your knees, just like a back squat. The upright torso makes depth feel natural for most lifters, and full depth builds the most strength.

faqItems.question: How many reps should I do on the front squat?
faqItems.answer: Sets of 3 to 5 reps work well for strength. Longer sets are harder to keep clean because the upper back tires before the legs do, so add sets rather than reps when you want more volume.
